headline: Approved June 17 minutes; discussed inclusionary zoning changes, a CPC funding application, and housing projects at 213 Main Street and 245 Bryant Street.
summary: The June 17, 2026 minutes were approved unanimously. Mollie Ping was introduced as the new Housing Programs Coordinator. Staff also gave updates on a finance report, proposed inclusionary zoning changes, a CPC funding application, and several housing projects.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the June 17, 2026 meeting unanimously.

Mayor Christenson presented the following remote meeting notice into the  record:
On March 28, 2025, Governor Maura Healey signed legislation extending certain
COVID-19 relief measures including extending remote meetings for public bodies.  The
same provisions which permitted multiple-member bodies to meet remotely, or 
convene in a hybrid manner, have been extended through June 30, 2027.  This 
extension allows public bodies to continue to meet remotely or to meet in a hybrid 
manner, without a quorum of the public body physically present at a meeting location,
as long as the public body provides "adequate, alternative" means of access to remote
meetings. This meeting will be conducted via remote participation. This meeting will 
not include in-person attendance by members of the public, but all effort will be made
to permit public attendance, in the manner specified below, via remote access by 
internet, and telephone. Public access will also be provided by posting draft minutes, 
and/or a transcript, recording, or record of the meeting on the City of Malden website
at cityofmalden.org as soon as practicable after the meeting.

Paul Goldstein called the roll at 5:03pm. Mayor Christenson confirmed next meeting is on 
Wednesday, October 21st at 5:00pm.
 Mayor Christenson, Councilor Linehan, Angie Liou, Catherine Price, and Steve Finn 
were present. Roxanne Reddington-Wilde joined late.
 Others Present: Paul Goldstein, Mollie Ping, Jane Ventrone (OSPCD staff), Dan Grover 
(Treasurer) 
2. New AHTF staff introduction (Mollie Ping, Housing Programs Coordinator)
 Paul Goldstein introduced Mollie Ping as the new Housing Programs Coordinator. Mollie
Ping expressed excitement about new role and provided that before this role, she worked 
as a graduate school co-op in the Development Review division of the City of Boston’s 
Planning Department. 
3. Approval of Meeting Minutes from June 17, 2026.
On a motion by Angie Liou, seconded by Councilor Linehan, the minutes from the 
June 17, 2026 meeting were approved unanimously.
4. Finance Report
Dan Grover was in attendance to deliver the Finance Report:
The current Trust account balance is $2,071,277.32 inclusive June, July, August interest 
in the amounts of $5,416.51, $6,148.79 and $6,148.68 respectively. The regularly 
reported expenses are June, July and August salary related expenses of $3,726.28 
applied, there may be additional expense related items posted upon receipt of details.   No
operating expenses currently encumbered.  On May 6, 2026 the Mayor signed Paper 213 
of 2026 appropriating $500,000.00 from the CPA to the Affordable Housing Trust 
Fund.  That $500k has been transferred to the AHTF account. Current interest rate is 
350bps or 3.50% that is an increase of 50 basis points over last repot in May.  We can 
anticipate roughly $72k in interest per annum or $6,000 a month at 3.50.  We are still 
participating in the Eastern Bank IntraFi Cash Service or Sweep agreement with Eastern 
Bank to mitigate risk and extract yield.            
Approved funding recommendations from Oct 2023, Feb 2025, Nov 2025 meetings 
respectively yet to be spent:

5. Administrative Updates
a. Inclusionary Zoning-ordinance update and related information
- Mollie Ping delivered Inclusionary Zoning updates. Noted that these changes were 
introduced to encourage more development of inclusionary zoning projects. The last 
significant updates were 5 years ago, and the ordinance sets out a look-back period of

5 years bringing us now to this proposal. Our team is strategizing how to best move 
forward these changes after receiving feedback from the planning board and city 
council. As a reminder, the updates refer to a few notable proposed changes 
including: 
o Reducing the portion of units set aside for IZ from 15% to 10% in new 
multifamily projects with 8 or more units. This is proposed to boost more 
housing development in Malden. As it currently stands with a 15% 
requirement, developers do not see significant internal rates of returns on their
investments, and we feel hopeful that lowering the requirement to 10% will 
encourage more development. 
o Reducing mandatory parking minimums for projects complying with the 
Inclusionary Zoning ordinance. Currently, there is 1 parking space per 
bedroom that is built. We propose 1 space per unit for market-rate and mixed-
income projects and 1 space per unit of affordable housing, which is up from 
the 0.75 spots per unit. In our research we found that current parking 
mandates limit size availability for housing development and exceed local 
needs. 
o Increasing the density bonus for developers who comply with IZ ordinance 
from 1:1 to 2:1. This will hopefully make building affordable housing more 
attractive to developers.
- These changes went to Rules and Ordinance committee last night and it looks like it 
will go back to this same committee week after next. It does not look like we need to 
go back to the full council. 
Roxanne asked how it would work for a 0.8 unit in an 8-unit building, Paul responded 
that rounding up to 1 unit is usually the protocol for this. Roxanne also asked for 
clarification on the ratio changes. Paul responded that the developer could provide an 
additional unit of housing through maximizing the space.
b. CPC Funding Application
Paul provided an update that OSPCD staff has submitted an application to the 
CPC on behalf of the Trust for FY26 CPA funds. We anticipate the application to 
be considered sometime in the next couple of months, likely in November. If 
additional letters of support or other testimony is needed from the Trust, staff will 
be sure to reach out accordingly. 
6. Affordable Housing Program Updates
a. Office of Housing Stability
Mollie Ping provided an update on behalf of the Office of Housing Stability 
(OHS). Through a partnership with the United Way, OHS helped 10 Malden 
households with utility arrears. Additionally, OHS helped a homeowner get 
caught up on property taxes. OHS secured gift cards for 3 households from a local
furniture company.
Last year, OHS partnered with New England Law School to run an Eviction 
Sealing Clinic for tenants, and OHS is pleased to report that they will be running 
the clinic again this year.

b. Development Projects
 Overlook Ridge (Winn Development)
Winn Development has been working with MassHousing on a homeownership tax
credit application for lot 14B, which is now planned for 50 units. MassHousing 
has asked that Winn further the design for the smaller scale of the project and also
work on going through the permitting process for the new design. Site Plan 
Approval modification and requested changes to the Special Permit are underway,
with formal submissions to be made this month. 
For lot 13B, the affordable rental portion of the development, Winn will be 
applying for funds to EOHLC sometime in 2027.
Mayor is cautiously optimistic about this project moving forward. Roxanne asks why they
had to reduce the number of homeownership buildings, Paul says that homeownership 
funds are oversaturated at the state-level so the developer decided to scale back to rental 
units. 
 105 Salem Street (Volunteers of America)
Mollie has check-in with Matt on Thursday to get more updates on project. Still 
waiting to hear back from MassDevelopment on application for funds from their 
Underutilized Properties Program which is their last funding source they are 
seeking for the project.
 245 Bryant Street (Asian Community Development Corporation)
ACDC is continuing to pursue the necessary permits for its 245 Bryant Street 
project, which will now be an all-affordable rental development with 36 units. 
The Planning Board still needs to approve ACDC’s proposed amendment to the 
special permit it received from the Board last year. ACDC is also in the process of
pursuing other public funding sources for the project from EOHLC and recently 
secured $1.1 million commitment of HOME funds from the City of Malden from 
the NSC. ACDC has not applied for Trust funds yet, but this could change 
depending on cost increases and the availability of other public funds.
 213 Main Street (Asian Community Development Corporation)
Weekly closing calls are ongoing the target closing date is November 2nd. 
However, ACDC is hoping to begin some preliminary site work sometime in 
October.
7. Adjournment
Roxanne Reddington-Wilde made a motion to adjourn and was seconded by 
Catherine Price. Mayor initiated a final roll call of Trustees. All Trustees 
voted in favor and the meeting was adjourned at 5:29 PM.
